sentences.text: It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that victim is a consenting party and no case for the alleged offences is [2024:RJ-JD:8167] (2 of 5) [CRLMB-1348/2024] made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4. I have considered the submissions made by both the parties and perused the material made available to the Court.
5. The victim is a young lady of 28 years and is residing at Bhilwara (Rajasthan) since a considerable long time.

She submitted a report on 10.09.2023 at the Police Station Subhash Nagar, Bhilwara alleging therein that in the Year 2008 when she was a minor girl and travelling in a train with her family from Mumbai to Bhilwara, he started talking to her family and asked for a job for himself at Bhilwara.
Thereafter, he exchanged his mobile number.
She also stated that the accused used to made calls to her and her family members.
It is alleged that in the Year 2008 she was forcibly taken away by the accused to Delhi and she was forced to convert her religion for which she confined in a house at Mangolpuri, Delhi.
It is further alleged that accused established physical relations with her and as a consequence of fornication, she got conceived and on 23.01.2010 she delivered a male child named Anshul.

It is alleged by her that she was subjected to rape by the other family members of the petitioner, however, in the report the victim has neither disclosed that on what date, day,
[2024:RJ-JD:8167] (3 of 5) [CRLMB-1348/2024] time and place she was subjected to rape by the members of the petitioner's family nor such allegations were made by her in the statement recorded by the Investigating Officer.

She further alleged she was subjected to cruelly by them however,
claims that as an outcome of the illicit relationship between, on 31.12.2017, she begotten a female child named Anshika and whereafter probably, she returned back to her parental home at Bhilwara but when she came back, she did not disclose the same anywhere.
She alleged that when she returned back to her parental home, she was regularly receiving threat from the accused on phone calls.

Lastly, she alleged that on 23.01.2023, the accused petitioner came to her house i.e. Chandra Shekhar Azad Nagar, Bhilwara and subjected her to rape with a threat that she will not disclose their relationship to anyone otherwise, he will kill her children.

6. After lodging of the aforesaid FIR, the agency conducted usual investigation and a notice under Section 91 of the Cr.P.C. was given to her for furnishing requisite documents, however, for most of them, she denied.
Interestingly, when she was examined under Section 164 Cr.P.C. by a Judicial Magistrate at Bhilwara, she resiled from the allegations of subjecting her to rape on 23.01.2023 at Bhilwara.

It would be worthwhile to mention here that upon her missing in the Year 2008, her father Rama Shanker Singh lodged a Missing Person Report in which it was stated that his daughter left the home without informing him.
Now, her both children namely Anshul and Anshika have grown up and presently aged 13 years and 6 years respectively and residing with her at [2024:RJ-JD:8167] (4 of 5) [CRLMB-1348/2024] Bhilwara.

sentences.text: pondering over the issue, prima facie, it is felt that it is a case of matrimonial strife between the parties, however, neither the same is a finding nor an adjudication on the issue by this Court rather it is felt appropriate to leave it to the learned trial Court to adjudicate upon the same after taking entire evidence on record.

At present, it can be considered that the petitioner is behind the bars and the report in this case came to be lodged on 10.09.2023 for the incident which happened in the Year 2008 for which, no satisfactory explanation has been furnished by the victim.

She; as per her allegation managed to free from the clutches of the accused in the year 2017-18 but till the year 2023, not lodging any report by her crime further create a serious doubt over the genuineness of the allegations and at this stage, the submission of the defence regarding possibility of embellishment,
concoction or false implication cannot be ruled out.
This fact also cannot be overlooked that she delivered two issues out of cohabitation with the Petitioner.

Her deviation, retraction from earlier statement and incongruity appearing in her stand persuading this Court to take a lenient view in a bail application filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
7.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and after minutely going through the niceties of the matter, at present, I see no reason to allow further incarceration of the petitioner while leaving the issues to be adjudicated by the learned trial Court during the course of trial as granting bail would not mean absolving the accused from the charges.

There is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude, [2024:RJ-JD:8167] (5 of 5) [CRLMB-1348/2024]
therefore, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.
8.
It is nigh well settled law that at a pre-conviction stage; bail is a rule and denial from the same should be an exception.
The purpose behind keeping an accused behind the bars during trial would be to secure his presence on the day of conviction so that he may receive the sentence as would be awarded to him.
Otherwise, it is the rule of Crimnal Jurisprudence that he shall be presumed innocent until the guilt is proved.

9. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

10. Before parting, it is made clear that any observation made herein above are limited to the extent of justifiable disposal of instant bail application which would have no bearance on the merits of the case and shall not influence the trial Judge at any stage of trial.

(FARJAND ALI),J 90-Mamta/-
